Investing.com - Jefferies downgraded Bill.com Holdings Inc. (NYSE:BILL) to Hold from Buy and raised its price target to $63.25 from $62.00 on Friday.

Bill.com announced a definitive agreement to be acquired by TPG, in partnership with Corpay, for $63.25 per share in an all-cash transaction. The deal values the company at approximately $6.0 billion on a fully diluted equity basis and represents a 29% premium to its 50-day moving average. The stock surged 17.6% over the past week and is trading near its 52-week high of $66.58, according to InvestingPro data, which indicates the stock remains undervalued based on its Fair Value analysis.

TPG Capital will own a majority interest following the transaction, with Corpay acquiring a minority interest. Corpay will invest $1.1 billion for approximately one-third equity stake in Bill.com, along with the option to acquire 100% of the company.

The transaction was unanimously approved by Bill.com’s Board. There are no financing conditions associated with the transaction.

The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, subject to shareholder approval, regulatory approvals and customary closing conditions. For deeper insights into Bill.com’s financial health and valuation, investors can access the comprehensive Pro Research Report, available for this and 1,400+ other US equities on InvestingPro.

In other recent news, Bill.com Holdings Inc. announced an agreement to be acquired by TPG in partnership with Corpay for $6.0 billion, or $63.25 per share, marking a 31% premium to the 60-day weighted average price through November 16. Following this announcement, Oppenheimer downgraded Bill.com to Perform from Outperform. Similarly, Susquehanna downgraded Bill.com to Neutral from Positive, citing uncertainty surrounding the merger and acquisition activities, despite noting the company’s strong operational performance with a 38.7% adjusted operating margin and multiyear high payment volume growth.

In contrast, BMO Capital raised its price target for Bill.com shares to $68 from $56, maintaining a Market Perform rating, due to ongoing acquisition speculation. Truist Securities also increased its price target to $58 from $50 after Bill.com’s first-quarter fiscal 2027 earnings report, which led to a slight upward revision in their fiscal 2027 core revenue forecast. Additionally, William Blair upgraded Bill.com to Outperform from Market Perform, highlighting the company’s strong position as a leading B2B provider with potential for improved monetization and margin expansion. These developments reflect a mix of reactions from analysts regarding Bill.com’s recent activities and future prospects.
